696.1: Raag Jaitsri, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The jewel of the Lord's Name has come to dwell in my heart; the Guru has laid his hand upon my forehead. The sins and sorrows of birth after birth have been lifted away; the Guru has given the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered), and the debt is cleared. O my mind, worship with love the Name of Ram: in it are all the things one seeks. The Perfect Guru has fixed the Lord's Name firmly within; without the Name, life is in vain. Without the Guru, the manmukhs (the self-willed) are left fools; they are ever caught in attachment to Maya. They have never served the feet of the Saadh (the Guru); their whole life goes for nothing. Those who have served the Saadh's feet, the feet of the holy, have made their life fruitful; they are no longer without a Master. Make me the servant of the servants of your servants, O Lord, Master of the world (Jagannath), in your mercy. We are blind, without wisdom and unknowing: how are we to walk upon the way, the path? O Guru, give us, the blind, the hem of your robe, so that we, servant Nanak, may walk on holding fast to it. ॥4॥
Chaupade (chau, four; pad, stanza): hymns of four stanzas.
696.2: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). A diamond, a ruby, is priceless and of great weight; yet without a buyer it counts for no more than a straw. When the jewel's buyer, the Guru, the Saadh, came into sight, then the jewel sold for lakhs. The Lord had kept a hidden diamond (the Name) within my mind. The One merciful to the meek brought me to the Guru, the Saadh; on meeting the Guru, I knew the diamond for what it is. In the chamber (of the heart) of the manmukhs is the darkness of ignorance; they have not discerned the jewel in their own home. Those fools have died astray in the wilds, for they have tasted the venom of the serpent Maya. O Lord, Har Har, unite us with the Saadhs, your good servants; O Lord, keep us in the refuge of the Saadh (the Guru). O Lord, O God, my Master, take us as your own; we have fled and fallen at your side. Which of your virtues can we tell and describe with our tongue? You are great and beyond reach, the great Being. The Lord has shown mercy to servant Nanak; the Lord has saved the sinking stone. ॥4॥
697.1: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). We children know nothing of your state and your extent (what you are and how great); we are your foolish, simple, ignorant ones. O Lord, in your mercy give a noble understanding, and make this fool wise. My idle mind had sunk into drowsiness. The Lord, Har Har, has brought the Guru, the Saadh, and united me with him; meeting the Saadh, the doors (of the mind) have swung open. O Guru, kindle love in my heart moment by moment; my Beloved's Name is my very breath of life. Without the Name one dies, my Master, as an addict craves for his drug. Those in whose minds love for the Lord has taken hold: theirs is the fortune written of old, from the very start. Moment by moment we serve the feet of those who find the Lord sweet. My Master, the Lord, Har Har, has shown grace, and has united with himself the servant long separated. Blessed, blessed is the True Guru, who has fixed the Name firmly within; servant Nanak is a sacrifice to him. ॥4॥
Kapat here is kapaat, doors or shutters (the Darpan, the Faridkot Teeka), not kapat, deceit.
697.2: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). I have found the True Guru, my friend, the great Being; with relish upon relish the fruit of the Lord has come to me. The serpent Maya has seized the mortal; through the Guru's words the Lord draws out the poison. My mind is held by the sweet essence of the Lord's Name. The Lord has made the fallen pure; meeting the Guru, the Saadh, they have tasted the Lord's sweet essence in the Lord's Name. Blessed, blessed is the great good fortune by which the Guru, the Saadh, is met; meeting the Saadh, the attention rests in the state of unman (the mind raised above the world). The fire of craving is quenched and peace is found, singing the pure, the utterly pure virtues of the Lord. Meagre was the fortune set from the start for those who have not had the sight of the True Guru. In the love of another they fall into womb after womb; their whole life passes in vain. O Lord, give a spotless understanding, that we may serve the feet of the Guru, the Saadh, and the Lord may seem sweet to us. Servant Nanak begs for the dust of the Saadh's feet; the Lord, becoming merciful, has it given. ॥4॥
697.3: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Those in whose hearts the Lord's Name has not come to dwell: better the Lord had made their mothers barren. Their bodies wander empty, without the Name; they have worn themselves away and died, fretting and pining. O my mind, repeat the Name of Ram, the Lord who dwells within. The merciful Lord God, Har Har, showed mercy; the Guru gave wisdom, and the mind understood. In Kalyug the Lord's praise is the highest state; it is through the True Guru that the Lord is found. I give myself in sacrifice to my own True Guru, who has brought the hidden Name to light. By great fortune the sight of the Saadh (the Guru) was granted, and all sins are lost and gone. I have found the True Guru, the banker great in wisdom, who has made me a sharer in the Lord's many virtues. Those on whom the Life of the world has shown mercy have enshrined the Lord in their hearts, within their minds. At the door of Dharam Raj their papers were torn up; O servant Nanak, their account is settled. ॥4॥
Kalyug: in the reckoning of the Puranas, the fourth and darkest of the world's four ages, held to be the present one.
Dharam Raj judges each soul by its deeds; the papers are the record of deeds written at his door.
698.1: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). By great fortune I have found the Sat Sangat (the company of the true) of the Saadh (the Guru); my wandering mind has come to rest. Instruments ever play with the unstruck (anhat) melody; (the mind) has drunk its fill, with love, of the stream of the Lord's Amrit. O my mind, repeat the Name of Ram, the beautiful Lord. The True Guru has kindled love in my mind and body; the Lord has met me and clasped me in his embrace. The Saakats (those who have turned from God) are bound fast in Maya; they hoard poison with all their might. They cannot spend it for the Lord's sake, and they bear the pain of Jamkaal (death) upon their heads. Those who have given their bodies over to the Lord, applying with deep faith the dust (of the feet) of the Guru, the Saadh, to their faces, win glory from the Lord in this world and the next; the deep colour of the Lord's love has dyed their minds. O Lord, Har Har, unite me, unite me with your servant, the Saadh (the Guru); I am a worm (a lowly servant) of the holy ones. O servant Nanak, (one whose) love has taken hold for the feet of the Guru, the Saadh: meeting the Saadh, (that one's) foolish mind of stone has turned green. ॥4॥
Saakat (Sanskrit shakta): a worshipper of Shakti (Maya); in Gurbani, one cut off from God and lost in Maya.
The anhat (anāhata, unstruck) melody is the sound made by no striking: the divine music that sounds unbroken through all creation.
698.2: Raag Jaitsri, Ghar 2, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Remember the Lord, Har Har, the unreachable, the infinite, remembering whom our pain is erased. O Lord, Har Har, unite (us) with the True Guru, the Being; when the Guru is met, there is peace. Sing the Lord's virtues, my friends; keep the Name of the Lord, Har Har, enshrined in the heart. Recite to (me) the Amrit words of the Lord, Har Har; when the Guru is met, (the Lord) becomes manifest. The Lord, Madhusudan, Madho, is my breath of life; to my mind and body (his) Amrit tastes sweet. O Lord, Har Har, show mercy and unite (me) with the Guru, that Being untouched by Maya (Niranjan). The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is ever the giver of peace; my mind is dyed in the Lord's love. O Lord, Har Har, unite (me) with the Guru, the great Being; says Nanak: O Guru, through the Name there is peace. ॥4॥
Ram at the end of many lines of these shabads is a sung word of the measure, a calling on the Lord; it is not rendered.
Madhusudan (the slayer of the demon Madhu): a name of Vishnu; in Gurbani, a name of God. Madho (maa, Maya or Lakshmi, and dhav, husband): a name of God.
698.3: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, Har Har; through the Guru, ever earn the profit of the Naam. Make devotion to the Lord, Har Har, firm within; the Name of the Lord, Har Har, (fills the mind with) eager delight. Meditate on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, the merciful; in the Lord's love, ever sing (his) virtues. Dance the ghoomar of the praise of the Lord, Har Har; joining the Sat Sangat, there is eager delight. Come, my companions, let us meet in union with the Lord; hearing the Lord's discourse, earn the profit of the Naam. Show mercy, O Lord, Har Har, and unite (us) with the Guru; when the Guru is met, there is eager delight for the Lord. Singing the praise and glory of the unreachable, the unfathomable (Lord), sing the Name of Ram at every moment. O Guru, the giver, show mercy and meet me; Nanak's eager delight is in devotion to the Lord. ॥4॥
Ghoomar: a women's dance, whirling round in a circle.
Umaha (spelt ਓੁਮਾਹਾ, read umaha): eager delight, joyful longing; most stanzas of these shabads end on it.
699.1: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). With delight upon delight we praise the Lord (Ram), the fount of all sweetness; the mind is drenched in the Lord's Name and earns the profit. Moment by moment, day and night, we perform devotion; through the Guru's teaching there is eager delight in devotion. We repeat the virtues of Govind (the Lord of the universe), the Lord, Har Har; conquering mind and body, we earn the profit of the Shabad. Through the Guru's teaching the five enemies (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) come under control; in mind and body there is eager delight for the Lord. The Naam is a jewel; we repeat the Lord's Name; singing the Lord's virtues, we ever earn the profit. O Madho, merciful to the meek, show mercy, (that there may be) eager delight for the Name of the Lord, Har Har. Again and again I repeat (the Name of) the Lord of the world (Jagdish) within my mind; the Lord, Har Har, the Master of the world, is the (true) profit in the world. Blessed, blessed are you, my great Master, my God; repeating (your Name), Nanak has eager delight in devotion. ॥4॥
699.2: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). He himself is the yogi, and the way (of yoga), through all the ages; he himself, the fearless, sits rapt in trance. He himself alone is at work in all; he himself (gives) eager delight in the Name. He himself is the continents (dweep) and the worlds, and he gives them light; he himself is the True Guru and the ocean, and he churns it. He himself, churning and churning, has the essence drawn out; repeating the jewel of the Name, there is eager delight. Come together, my companions; together let us sing (his) virtues; through the Guru, repeat the Naam: (this is) the profit of the Lord. (One in whom) devotion to the Lord, Har Har, is made firm and is pleasing to the mind: (to that one) the Name of the Lord, Har Har, brings eager delight. He himself is the great, wise one, the great banker; through the Guru, buy the capital of the Naam. O Lord, Har Har, O God, grant this gift, as it pleases you: for Nanak, (your) virtues, (your) Name and eager delight (in it). ॥4॥
699.3: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Joining the Sat Sangat, in the company of the Guru, let us buy, through the Guru, the capital of the Naam. O Lord, Har Har, O Madhusudan, show mercy, that joining the Sat Sangat, there may be eager delight. May we hear with our ears the Bani of the Lord's virtues; in your mercy, unite (us) with the True Guru. May we sing (your) virtues and speak (your) virtues through the Bani; repeating the Lord's virtues, there is eager delight. If all pilgrimages, fasts, sacrificial rites and acts of charity are weighed, they never come up to the Name of the Lord, Har Har. Beyond all weighing is the Lord, Har Har; his weight is exceedingly great; repeating (him) through the Guru's teaching, there is eager delight. May we repeat the Lord's Name: (it is) all rites and righteous deeds; (it) washes away the filth of sins and misdeeds. O you who are merciful to the meek, be kind to your servant; give Nanak the Name and eager delight (in it). ॥4॥
700.1: Raag Jaitsri, Ghar 3, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Rare is the one who knows who is a (true) friend here in this world. Only one on whom (God) is merciful understands the way of it; that one's way of life is pure. Mother, father, wife, sons, kin, dear friends and brothers have come together through the ties of past births; at the end, none of them is any help. Strings of pearls, gold, rubies and diamonds, the wealth that charms the mind: crying out for (them), one's span of life has passed, yet in them no contentment was found. Elephants, chariots, horses swift as the wind, (one may be) a man of wealth, a lord of lands, (master of) an army of four wings, yet none of these went along with him at all; he rose and departed naked. The Lord's Sants are the dear beloveds of God; in their company one should sing (the praise of) the Lord, Har Har. O Nanak, peace here and a radiant face hereafter are found in the company of the Sants. ॥4॥
An army of four wings (chaturanga): elephants, chariots, horsemen and foot soldiers.
700.2: Raag Jaitsri, Ghar 3, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Give me word, tell me, tell me of the Beloved. Hearing (of him) in so many ways, I am bewildered; tell me, O happy soul-brides, my companions. Some say he is outside all, far beyond; some say he is within all. No colour of his is seen, no mark of his is discerned; O happy soul-brides, help me understand the truth. He dwells in all, he lives in every heart, and yet no stain touches him, not in the least. Says Nanak: listen, O people, he dwells upon the tongue of the Sants. ॥2॥
Dupade (du, two; pad, stanza): hymns of two stanzas.
Suhagan (the happy soul-bride): one whose Husband, the Lord, is with her; here, those who have already met God.
700.3: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Hearing of God, I take heart, I take heart. Seeing God near, close at hand, I offer (him) my soul, my breath, my mind, my body, everything. He is countless, endless, the great Giver; seeing God, I hold him fast in my mind. Whatever I wish for, that very thing I receive; meditating on God, I fulfil my hopes and longings. By the Guru's grace (God) has come to dwell in Nanak's mind; having understood God, I never pine in any sorrow. ॥4॥
700.4: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). My Friend is the one for whom (all) long. In every home sing beautiful songs of joy (to him); in every heart he has his dwelling. Worship him in joy, worship him in sorrow; may he not be forgotten at any time. Repeating the Naam brings the light of millions of suns, and doubt's darkness is destroyed. (O God,) in every place and every space between, in all places (you are); whatever is seen is yours. O Nanak, whoever finds (God) in the company of the Sants never again goes round (in birth and death). ॥2॥
701.1: Raag Jaitsri, Ghar 4, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Now I have found peace by the Guru's command. I have given up cleverness, put worry out of mind, and cast off ego and left it behind. When I look, I see all bewitched by attachment; so I ran and fell at the Guru's refuge. In his mercy the Lord set me to his service; then Jam (the messenger of Death) let go of me. I crossed the ocean of fire when, by great fortune, I met the Sants. Servant Nanak has found every comfort, for my mind is fixed on the Lord's feet. ॥2॥
701.2: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I have fixed my attention on the True Guru in my mind; I have made firm (within me) the wisdom and the mantra of the Lord's Name; God has shown me mercy. The nets of death, the great entanglements and the fear of Jam are gone. I have come to the refuge of the remover of sorrow, the Lord of compassion, and have taken hold of (his) feet as (my) support. The Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) has become a boat, (and I) have crossed the ocean of the world. Says Nanak, I have drunk the Amrit (of the Name), doubt is gone, and I have borne the unbearable. ॥2॥
Ajar jara: to bear the unbearable, holding with composure the state the Name brings.
701.3: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Those for whom Govind has become the helper have every comfort, Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise) and bliss with them; no ailment touches them. They are seen with everyone, yet stay untouched; Maya has no hold on them. Dyed in the love of the One, they know the essence; they have received this understanding from the True Guru. Those on whom the Master's kindness, compassion and grace rest are the Sants of loving heart. O Nanak, in the company of those who have sung the Lord's praises with relish and delight, one is carried across. ॥2॥
701.4: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Gobind, you are the life, the breath, the wealth and the beauty (of all beings); for creatures sunk deep in ignorance and attachment, you are a lamp in the darkness. O beloved God, the sight of you bears fruit; (your) lotus feet are beyond compare. Countless times I bow to them, and offer my very mind (before them) as incense. Worn out, I have fallen at your door, O God, and have taken firm hold of your shelter. Pull Nanak, your own, out of the pit of the world's fire. ॥2॥
701.5: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). If only some servant (of God) would join me to the Lord, I would clasp his feet, speak kind words (to him) with my tongue, and my very life would be given (to him) as an offering. (A rare one) makes mind and body a pure garden-bed and waters it well with the Lord's nectar; by (God's) grace, breaking away from the great poison of Maya, he is absorbed in this relish. O destroyer of the sorrows of the meek, I have come to your refuge; I turn my thoughts to you (alone). O God, undo Nanak's bonds and (grant him) the gift of the fearless state and of the Master's remembrance. ॥2॥
702.1: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). As the chatrik longs for the rain to pour, (so I long:) O God, ocean of mercy, show compassion: (grant me) the longing for loving devotion to the Lord. The chakvi does not want countless comforts; seeing the day (break), she is in perfect bliss. By no other means does the fish live; without water, death is its lot. O Lord, O Master, we who have no master are at your refuge: show your mercy. Nanak worships (God's) lotus feet; without him, nothing else (is dear to him). ॥2॥

The chatrik (pied cuckoo) is held in Indian poetry to drink only the raindrop that falls under the Swati star, and no other water; the chakvi (ruddy shelduck) is parted from her mate at night and waits all night for the sunrise.
702.2: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). He who is my very life dwells in my mind and body; in his mercy the Perfect Being, the all-knowing, has met me in the company of the Saadh (the Guru). Those who have been given the stupefying herb of love have drunk the sweet essence in great measure. Its worth cannot be told; what power have I (to tell it)? (God) has fastened his servants to the hem of his robe; the Saviour has saved (them). Remembering, remembering, remembering God, Nanak has found peace at the refuge of (his) door. ॥2॥
Thagauri: the stupefying herb (datura and the like) that thugs gave travellers in order to rob them; here it is love, which leaves the mind lost to all else.
702.3: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). After wandering through countless births, we have come to (your) refuge. Save (us) from the blind well of (attachment to) the body, and attach (us) to your feet. I know nothing of wisdom, meditation or (righteous) deeds; my conduct is not pure. Attach (me) to the hem of the Saadh Sangat, so that the treacherous river may be crossed. Comforts, wealth, the sweet pleasures of Maya: these are not to be kept in the mind. Servant Nanak finds his fill in the sight of the Lord; the love of the Lord's Name is (his) ornament. ॥2॥
702.4: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O servants of the Lord, remember Ram in your hearts. Misfortune does not come near the Lord's servant; all the tasks of (such) a servant are fulfilled. Through the Lord's service millions of obstacles are destroyed, (and) the eternal abode of Govind (is reached). The devotee of the Lord has no fear at all; (even) Jam pays him honour. Forsaking Gopal (the Lord who sustains all), whatever else is done is unsound, and every bit of it perishes. O Nanak, hold (God's) lotus feet in your heart; (in them) all comforts find their home. ॥2॥
702.5: Raag Jaitsri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The mind has gone astray, entangled in Maya. Whatever deeds it did, driven by greed, by each of them it bound itself. It did not understand; absorbed in the pleasures of the senses, it forgot the Lord's praise. The Master is with it, but it did not know him; it ran off to search the forests. Ram, the jewel, is within the heart itself, yet it did not gain the knowledge of him. O servant Nanak, without worship of the Lord it has wasted its life in vain. ॥2॥
703.1: Raag Jaitsri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). O dear Lord, save my honour. The dread of Jam has entered my heart; O treasure of mercy, I have taken hold of your refuge. I am a great sinner, a fool, and greedy too; committing sins, I am now worn out. The fear of dying never leaves my mind; that worry has burnt up my body. I tried (many) means to be set free, and rose and ran in all ten directions. The Stainless One dwells within the heart itself, (yet) I have not found his secret. I have no virtue, no chanting or austerity at all; what deed should now be done? Nanak, worn out, has fallen at (your) refuge; O God, grant the gift of fearlessness. ॥3॥
703.2: Raag Jaitsri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). O mind, hold fast to this true reflection: know that without the Name of Ram this whole world is false. He whom the yogis searched for until they were worn out, and did not find his limit: recognise that Master as near you; he is beyond form and feature. The Name of the Lord is the purifier in the world, (yet) you have never kept it in mind. O you to whom the world bows, Nanak has fallen at (your) refuge; keep to your age-old way (of grace). ॥2॥
703.3: Raag Jaitsri, Ghar 1, a Chhant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Thirsting for (his) sight, day and night, every day, always, I think of him. O Nanak, opening the doors (of my mind), the Guru has united me with the Lord, my Friend. ॥1॥
703.4: Listen, my friend, my dear one: I make one request. I wander searching for that enchanting, darling Beloved. Tell me of that Beloved, and I would cut off my head and lay it (before you); let me have (his) sight even for a moment. My eyes are dyed in the colour of the Beloved's love; (without him) I cannot be at peace even for an instant. My mind is absorbed in God as the fish in water; I thirst like the chatrik. Servant Nanak has found the Perfect Guru, and all thirst is quenched. O friend, all the Beloved's companions (are such that) I am like none of them. O friend, each surpasses the other; in whose thoughts am I? (God's) many loved ones, each surpassing the other, always enjoy the delights (of union with him). Seeing them, a longing rises in my mind: when shall I find the treasure of virtues? To the one who has won my Darling's pleasure I would give my mind. Says Nanak, O happy soul-bride, hear my plea: tell me, let me see, what is the Husband like? O friend, the Husband does as he himself wills; he depends on no one at all. O friend, you have enjoyed (union with) the Darling: I ask you, tell me. You have found the Darling by losing self; (he is found by) the bride on whose forehead good fortune is (written). (The happy soul-bride says:) The Master took me by the arm and made me his own; he did not weigh my virtues and faults. (O Lord,) she whom you have adorned with the necklace of virtues and dyed in the deep red of (your love), on her everything looks lovely. O servant Nanak, blessed is that happy soul-bride with whom the Husband dwells. O friend, the wish I always made in my prayers, that I have received. The Groom I longed for has come, and the songs of rejoicing ring out. Great joy and delight have come; the Husband is kind and ever fresh in his love. By great fortune I found him; the Guru brought me (to him) in the true company of the Saadh. All my hopes and longings are fulfilled; the Beloved has clasped me in his embrace. Nanak prays: the wish I made in my prayers, that I have received by meeting the Guru. ॥4॥

In this chhant the soul-bride who seeks the Lord speaks with a friend of the Sangat who has met the Husband. Several words are of the Lahnda (western Punjabi) speech: mu I, me; hik one; dun than; maida my; denhia I would give; dikha I may see; ghidhi took; neesi not.
704.1: Raag Jaitsri, Ghar 2, a Chhant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. God is lofty, beyond reach and boundless; the Indescribable cannot be described. Nanak has come to the refuge of God, who has the power to protect. As you see fit, O Lord God, so protect (me): I am yours. How many can I count? My faults are countless. Countless are the faults, the sins and the rounds (they bring); every day, always, we go astray. We stay sunk in attachment to dreadful Maya; by your grace alone are we set free. In secret we commit grievous wrongs, (yet) God is nearer than the nearest. Nanak prays: show mercy, and pull (us) out of the whirlpools of the world-ocean. (God's) countless virtues cannot be assessed; lofty is the Name of God. This is Nanak's prayer: may (I,) who have no place, find a place. There is no other place; to whom else should one go? At all hours, with joined palms, one should meditate on that God. Meditating always on that God of ours, one receives what the mind desires. Giving up pride, attachment and the sin of (leaning on) another, one should fix one's attention on the One. Offering mind and body before God, one should erase all self. Nanak prays: (O God,) show mercy, (that we may) stay merged in (your) True Name. O mind, one should meditate on him in whose hands is every means. O Nanak, one should gather the wealth of the Name of Ram; it goes with one to the end. God alone is the dear companion; there is no other. He himself is in every place and every space between; he fills the water and the land. God the Master, the Giver to all, pervades the water, the land and the sky. Gopal, Gobind has no end; his virtues are endless: how can I count them? Hasten to the refuge of the Master, the bringer of peace; besides him there is none. Nanak prays: (O God,) the one on whom you show mercy obtains the Naam. Whatever I wished for in my mind, that I have received. Meditating on the Naam, Nanak (has found) all comforts. Now, joining the company of the Saadh (the Guru), the mind is set free. Those who through the Guru have taken up the Naam have had their light merge in the Light. Remembering the Lord's Name, (their) sins are erased; the burning is quenched, and (the mind) is filled. In his kindness (God) has taken them by the arm, made them his own and given them honour. The Lord has clasped them to himself and united them (with him); the pains of birth and death are burnt away. Nanak prays: (God) has shown mercy and united (them with himself) in an instant. ॥4॥
705.1: Raag Jaitsri, a Chhant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The world is a traveller passing through, yet it is smeared with pride; steeped in the colours of Maya, people commit countless sins. Sunk in greed, attachment and arrogance, they never think of death; sons, friends, dealings and wife: tending to these, their life slips by. When the days written for them are over, O mother, they suffer at the sight of Dharam Raj's messengers. The deeds they have done are not wiped away; O Nanak, the wealth of the Lord's Name they have not earned. They make countless efforts, but do not sing the Lord's Name; they wander through countless births, dying, being born and coming again. Beasts, birds, stones and trees: (such births) are beyond all counting. Whatever seed you sow, its fruits you will enjoy; each one receives what he himself has done. Those who lose the jewel of this life in a gamble are not pleasing to God himself. Nanak prays: led astray, they wander, and find no resting place even for an instant. Youth has gone by, and old age has seized its place and settled in; his hands tremble, his head wobbles, and his eyes no longer see. Nothing is seen by the eyes; without worship of the Lord, he leaves Maya behind and departs. They do not heed his word and throw dust on his head, those for whose sake he burned his mind and body. The love of the Lord (Sri Ram), boundless and all-pervading, did not dwell in his mind even for an instant. Nanak prays: like millions of sheets of paper (in a fire), this false (body) takes no time to perish. Nanak has come to the refuge of the lotus feet (of the Lord); God himself has carried (us) across the world, so full of fears and so hard to cross. Joining the Saadh Sangat, we worshipped Sridhar (the Lord); taking our side, dear God carried (us) across. The Lord accepted (us) and gave (us) the Name; he weighed nothing else (of ours). The treasure of virtues, the boundless Master, the One our mind longed for, we have found. Nanak prays: having eaten the food of the Lord's Name, we are satisfied forever. ॥4॥
Sridhar (he who holds Sri, Lakshmi): a name of Vishnu; in Gurbani, a name of God.
705.2: Raag Jaitsri Vaar: by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji), with saloks. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. At the beginning the Supreme God is present everywhere, in the middle present everywhere, and at the end present everywhere. The Sants remember the One who pervades all places; O Nanak, the Lord of the world is the destroyer of sins. ॥1॥

In this vaar each pauri is preceded by two saloks: the first in Sahaskriti, a Sanskrit-coloured idiom (simrant, they remember; parmesurah, the Supreme God), the second in plainer speech, often Lahnda (habh for sabh, all; vasando, dwelling).
706.1: In seeing, hearing and telling (of him), let the True One be fixed firmly in the mind; he pervades all places; O Nanak, merge in the love of the Lord. ॥2॥
706.2: Let the One Lord, Niranjan, be sung; he alone is within all. God is the Cause of creation, all-powerful; whatever he does comes to pass. In an instant he sets up and pulls down; there is none but him. He pervades the continents, the universes, the nether worlds, the islands and all the worlds. He alone understands whom (God) himself makes understand; that one is a pure servant. ॥1॥
706.3: (God) fashions the frame of beings and places them in the mother's womb; with every breath they remember him, O Nanak, and the great fire (of the womb) does not destroy them. ॥1॥
706.4: With your face down and your feet up, you dwelt in that dreadful place; says Nanak: why have you forgotten that Master, through whose Name you are saved? ॥2॥
706.5: Of blood and seed you sprouted, in the fire of the belly, upside down, unclean and in distress, in a dreadful, pitch-dark hell. Remembering the Lord, you did not burn (there); enshrine him in your mind, your body and your heart. The One who brought you safe out of that hard place, do not forget him even a little. Forgetting God there is never peace; you will depart having lost your life. ॥2॥
706.6: He grants the gifts the mind desires, and fulfils hopes everywhere; he destroys strife and suffering; O Nanak, remember that God: he is not far. ॥1॥
706.7: The One in whose company you enjoy all pleasures: let love be formed with him. May that Husband Lord, who fashioned the beautiful body, not be forgotten for an instant, O Nanak. ॥2॥
706.8: He gave (you) soul and breath, body and wealth; he gave delights to enjoy. He gave houses, mansions, chariots and horses, arranging happy circumstances. God, who is able to give, has given sons, wife, friends and servants. Remembering the Lord, body and mind turn green, and the pains of separation are lifted. In the Saadh Sangat, dwell on the Lord's virtues; (so) all ailments are destroyed. ॥3॥
706.9: People strive for their family and make countless endeavours for Maya, but are empty of loving devotion to the Lord; O Nanak, those who forget God are ghosts. ॥1॥
706.10: Broken is the love that was formed with another; O Nanak, the true way is to be steeped in (the love of) the Master. ॥2॥
706.11: When the (life) leaves it, the body turns to ash, and all call it a ghost; those with whom there was such love do not let it stay in the house even for an instant. He amassed wealth by doing wrong; of what use is it (now)? As one sows, so one reaps; this (body) is the field of deeds. The ungrateful have forgotten the Lord, and wander through births. ॥4॥
706.12: (They gain the fruit of) millions of gifts in charity and holy bathings, and of countless rites of cleansing and purity, who utter Har Har with the tongue, O Nanak; they are freed from all sins. ॥1॥
706.13: I piled up a great heap of firewood and set a little fire to it (and it all burned away); just so, O Nanak, when the True Husband Lord dwells in the mind, all sorrows are taken away. ॥2॥
707.1: Millions of sins, every one of them, perish in remembering the Lord's Name; the fruits the mind longs for are obtained by singing the Lord's virtues; the fears of birth and death are cut away, (and one gains) the true place that never moves. If it is so written from the beginning, one is absorbed in the Lord's feet. O God, show grace and keep (me) safe; Nanak is a sacrifice (to you). ॥5॥
707.2: Endless adornment of the home, delights in the mind, the relish of tastes: those creatures who (amid these) never remember (the Lord), O Nanak, are worms in filth. ॥1॥
707.3: Great pomp, everything there is, and fondness and attachment (for it) within: O Nanak, the one who forgets that Master, that body is dust. ॥2॥
707.4: A beautiful bed, countless comforts, pleasures and enjoyments in full; houses of gold, scented with sandalwood, set with pearls and diamonds; he enjoys the pleasures the mind desires, and has no worry at all; (yet if) that God does not come to mind, (such people are) worms in filth. Without the Lord's Name there is no peace; by what means can the mind be comforted? ॥6॥
707.5: In longing for the lotus feet (of the Lord), the one who has turned from the world searches in all ten directions; he renounces deceitful Maya, O Nanak, (and finds) the Saadh Sangat, the very form of bliss. ॥1॥
707.6: With the Master in my mind, I utter (his Name) with my mouth and roam all the worlds; says Nanak: all show is false; I live by hearing (his) true praise. ॥2॥
707.7: (One) lives in a broken-down hut, his clothes all in rags; he has no caste, no honour, no respect, and wanders in the wilderness; he has no friend or loved one, no wealth, no beauty, and no relation or kin at all; (yet) he is the king of the whole world, his mind soaked in the Lord's Name. By the dust of his (feet) the mind is saved, and God is well pleased. ॥7॥
707.8: Countless sports, the joys of kingship, beauty, the royal canopy and fly-whisk, and a seat upon the throne: the fools, blind with ignorance, are absorbed in these; O Nanak, the longings of Maya are a dream. ॥1॥
707.9: In a dream (one) enjoyed every pleasure, and attachment felt sweet; O Nanak, without the Name, beautiful Maya is a deception. ॥2॥
707.10: The fool has fixed his mind on a dream; (on waking) the kingdom, the pleasures and the enjoyments are forgotten, and awake, he is left babbling. His years have gone by as he chased after worldly business; his tasks were never completed; Maya has enticed him. What can the poor creature do, when (the Lord) himself has led him astray? ॥8॥
707.11: They may live in the realms of heaven and win the earth with its nine regions, (yet) if they forget the Lord, Gopal, O Nanak, those mortals roam a wilderness. ॥1॥
707.12: Amid millions of wonders and spectacles, (if) the Name does not come to his mind, O Nanak, that very place is equal to millions of hells, a wasteland. ॥2॥
707.13: They have taken a most terrible wilderness for a city; seeing false things, they have taken them for true; in lust, anger and ego they roam about crazed. When Jam's club struck the head, then they repented. Without the perfect divine Guru, a person wanders about like Satan. ॥9॥
708.1: Kingship is deceit, beauty is deceit, wealth is deceit, and so is pride of lineage; (people) amass poisonous Maya by fraud and wrongdoing, but, O Nanak, apart from the Lord, none (of these) go along (with anyone). ॥1॥
708.2: How I erred in looking: the colocynth (tumma) seemed beautiful to me; it does not fetch even half a cowrie; O Nanak, Maya does not go along with (anyone). ॥2॥
The colocynth (tumma) is a fruit fair to look at but very bitter. A cowrie (kaudi) shell was the smallest coin.
708.3: Why gather what does not go along when one departs? Say, why strive for that from which one must be parted? Forgetting the Lord, how can one be satisfied? The mind is not gladdened. Whoever leaves God and clings to another is sunk in hell. Be kind and merciful (O God), and let Nanak's fear be destroyed. ॥10॥
708.4: Not sweet are the comforts of kingship, not sweet the relish of enjoyments, not sweet the comforts of Maya; sweet is the Lord in the Saadh Sangat; to servant Nanak, sweet is the sight of God. ॥1॥
708.5: That love has taken hold by which the mind is dyed from within; (the mind) is pierced by the True Thing (the Name); O Nanak, that Master seems sweet. ॥2॥
708.6: Without the Lord nothing seems sweet to the devotees. All other tastes are insipid: they have tested this and seen. Ignorance, doubt and sorrow have been cut away, for the Guru has become (their) intercessor. (Their) mind is pierced through by the lotus feet (of the Lord), like the (fast) colour of madder. God is (their) soul, breath of life, body and mind; all falsehood has perished. ॥11॥
Majith (madder): a plant whose red dye never fades; in Gurbani, the image of lasting love.
708.7: Parted from water the fish does not live; nor does the chatrik, if it leaves the realm of the clouds; the deer, (drawn) by the sound, is pierced by the arrow; the bumblebee is bound, (drawn) by the flower's fragrance; (just so) the Sants are absorbed in the lotus feet (of the Lord); O Nanak, nothing else pleases them. ॥1॥
The deer is drawn by the hunter's music and shot; the bumblebee, lingering for the scent, is shut in the closing lotus.
708.8: If I see (your) face for the blink of an eye, I would not leave (you) to give my heart to another. O Nanak, (true) life is union with that Master, the Lord, the friend of the Sants. ॥2॥
708.9: As a fish without water: how can it stay alive? The chatrik, deprived of the raindrop: how can it be satisfied? The deer, pierced by the (hunter's) music, rises and runs towards it; the bumblebee, greedy for the scent of the flower, meets it and has itself caught. So do the Sants love the Lord; beholding the sight of him, they are filled. ॥12॥
708.10: Those who dwell on (the Lord's) lotus feet and worship (him) with every breath, who never forget the Name of the Imperishable: O Nanak, the Supreme God fulfils their hopes. ॥1॥
708.11: (The Lord) is stitched into (their) minds, and is not apart (from them) for an instant; O Nanak, that True Master fulfils (their) hope and ever watches over (them). ॥2॥
708.12: O Lord of the world, fulfil the hope of (me,) the one who hopes; O Gopal, O Gobind, meeting (you), one never grieves. Grant (me) the sight of you, there is a longing in (my) mind, so that (my) sorrows lift. May (my) body become pure with the dust of (your) feet. O Supreme Lord, O divine Guru, (may I) remain ever in your presence. ॥13॥
709.1: Those whose tongues utter the Name, whose ears hear the Amrit Shabad, and whose attention is on the Supreme Lord: Nanak is ever a sacrifice to them. ॥1॥
709.2: Without the one Master, all deeds are false. O Nanak, they alone are blessed who love the True One. ॥2॥
709.3: I am ever a sacrifice to those who hear the Lord's praises told. Perfect and foremost are those who bow their heads before God. Beautiful are those hands that write the praise of the boundless Lord. Holy and pure are the feet that walk on God's path. In the company of the Sants one is saved, and all suffering has gone. ॥14॥
709.4: When, by perfect good fortune, the destiny (written on the forehead) comes to light, the Lord is remembered, and the sight of Gopal is attained: O Nanak, fruitful is that moment. ॥1॥
709.5: I cannot put a price on (those) joys; they are beyond all measure. O Nanak, approved is that blessed hour in which my Beloved meets (me). ॥2॥
709.6: Tell (me), which is that time in which I may find God? Auspicious is that moment, that hour of union, in which the Lord of the world is met. Meditating on the Lord at all hours, may I fulfil the longing of (my) mind; by great good fortune may the Sat Sangat come about, and may I bow low and fall at (their) feet. In (my) mind is a thirst for the sight of (God); Nanak is a sacrifice (to him). ॥15॥
709.7: Gobind makes the fallen pure and removes every fault. O Nanak, the Lord is a mighty champion to those in his refuge who repeat Har, Har, Har. ॥1॥
709.8: The one who has given up all self-conceit and clings close to (God's) feet: his pain and fever have fled, O Nanak, as he beholds God. ॥2॥
709.9: Unite (me with you), O Merciful one; I have fallen at your door. Save (me), O you who are merciful to the meek; wandering, I have grown utterly weary. To love devotion is your age-old way, O Lord, and to save the fallen. Apart from you there is no one to take up my plea. O Merciful one, take hold of (my) hand (and draw me out of) the world-ocean. ॥16॥
709.10: The Merciful one saves the Sants, whose support is the Kirtan of Gopal. In the company of (such) Sants one becomes pure; O Nanak, (their) shelter is the Supreme God. ॥1॥
709.11: Neither sandalwood nor the moon nor the cool season can take away the (mind's) burning heat at all; O Nanak, one becomes cool (only) by repeating the Name of the Lord. ॥2॥
709.12: In the shelter of (the Lord's) lotus feet all (his) people have been saved. Hearing of Govind's glory, (their) minds have become fearless. It never runs short at all: (they) have gathered the wealth of the Naam. The company of the Sants is found through great merit. Meditate on the Lord at all hours, and listen to the Lord's praise every day. ॥17॥
709.13: (The Lord) shows mercy and takes away the pain (of the one who) utters the Name and the praise of the merciful Lord, the all-pervading Being: O Nanak, Maya does not stain (that one). ॥1॥
710.1: The blazing fire has been put out; God himself is the protector. O Nanak, repeat (the Name of) that God who created the earth. ॥2॥
710.2: Once God has become merciful, Maya does not take hold. Tens of millions of sins were destroyed by meditating on the one Lord. Bodies became pure, bathed in the dust of (his) servants' feet. Mind and body grew content on finding the perfect God. (Their) families have crossed over, and with them (their) people and all (their) line. ॥18॥
710.3: The Guru is Gobind, the Guru is Gopal; the Guru is Narayan, pervading all. The Guru is merciful, the Guru is mighty; O Nanak, the Guru lifts up the fallen. ॥1॥
710.4: The world-ocean is terrible and unfathomable; the Guru, the ship, has carried me across. O Nanak, perfect fortune lies in clinging to the True Guru's feet. ॥2॥
710.5: Blessed, blessed is the divine Guru, in whose company (the Name of) the Lord is repeated. When the Guru became merciful, all failings were hidden away. The Supreme Lord, the divine Guru, has raised the lowly to high places. Cutting the noose of Maya's pains, he has made (them) his own servants. With the tongue (they) have sung the virtues and the praise of the boundless Lord. ॥19॥
710.6: Only the One is seen, only the One is heard; only the One, the Lord (Narhar), is at work (in all). (We) beg for the gift of the Name; says Nanak, O merciful Being, show (us your) grace. ॥1॥
710.7: I serve the One, I keep the One in mind; my prayer is to the one Lord alone. (I) have gathered the merchandise and the wealth of the Name; O Nanak, this is the true capital. ॥2॥
710.8: God is merciful and boundless; this One alone pervades all. He himself is everything; whom could I name as a second? O God, you yourself give the gift, and you yourself receive it. All coming and going is your Hukam (your will and command); your own abode stands unshakeable. Nanak begs for this gift: in your grace, give (me) the Naam. ॥20॥
710.9: Raag Jaitsri, the hymns of the Bhagats. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O Master, I know nothing; I have sold (my) mind into the hands of Maya. You are called the Guru of the world, the Master; I am called a lustful one of Kalyug. These five have so corrupted my mind that moment by moment they set a distance (between me and) the dear Lord. Wherever I look, there is a heap of pain; even now (my mind) is not convinced, though the Vedas bear witness. Gautam's wife (Ahalya), and the lord Shiva, husband of Uma, who bore (Brahma's severed) head, and (Indra,) who came to bear a thousand marks of the female organ: (all were brought low by these five). These demons have beaten the fool (of a mind) mercilessly, (yet it is) utterly shameless; even now it has not grown weary (of them). Says Ravidas: where can one go, what can one do? Without Raghunath (the Lord), whose refuge can one seek? ॥6॥
These five: lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride, which draw the mind away from God.

Stories of the Puranas: Indra sinned with Ahalya, the wife of the sage Gautam, and Gautam's curse left his body marked with a thousand marks of the female organ. When Brahma lusted after his own daughter, Shiva cut off his fifth head, and the head clung to Shiva's hand.

696.1: Raag Jaitsri, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The jewel of the Lord's Name has come to dwell in my heart; the Guru has laid his hand upon my forehead.
The sins and sorrows of birth after birth have been lifted away; the Guru has given the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered), and the debt is cleared.
O my mind, worship with love the Name of Ram: in it are all the things one seeks.
The Perfect Guru has fixed the Lord's Name firmly within; without the Name, life is in vain.
Without the Guru, the manmukhs (the self-willed) are left fools; they are ever caught in attachment to Maya.
They have never served the feet of the Saadh (the Guru); their whole life goes for nothing.
Those who have served the Saadh's feet, the feet of the holy, have made their life fruitful; they are no longer without a Master.
Make me the servant of the servants of your servants, O Lord, Master of the world (Jagannath), in your mercy.
We are blind, without wisdom and unknowing: how are we to walk upon the way, the path?
O Guru, give us, the blind, the hem of your robe, so that we, servant Nanak, may walk on holding fast to it. ॥4॥
696.2: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
A diamond, a ruby, is priceless and of great weight; yet without a buyer it counts for no more than a straw.
When the jewel's buyer, the Guru, the Saadh, came into sight, then the jewel sold for lakhs.
The Lord had kept a hidden diamond (the Name) within my mind.
The One merciful to the meek brought me to the Guru, the Saadh; on meeting the Guru, I knew the diamond for what it is.
In the chamber (of the heart) of the manmukhs is the darkness of ignorance; they have not discerned the jewel in their own home.
Those fools have died astray in the wilds, for they have tasted the venom of the serpent Maya.
O Lord, Har Har, unite us with the Saadhs, your good servants; O Lord, keep us in the refuge of the Saadh (the Guru).
O Lord, O God, my Master, take us as your own; we have fled and fallen at your side.
Which of your virtues can we tell and describe with our tongue? You are great and beyond reach, the great Being.
The Lord has shown mercy to servant Nanak; the Lord has saved the sinking stone. ॥4॥
697.1: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
We children know nothing of your state and your extent (what you are and how great); we are your foolish, simple, ignorant ones.
O Lord, in your mercy give a noble understanding, and make this fool wise.
My idle mind had sunk into drowsiness.
The Lord, Har Har, has brought the Guru, the Saadh, and united me with him; meeting the Saadh, the doors (of the mind) have swung open.
O Guru, kindle love in my heart moment by moment; my Beloved's Name is my very breath of life.
Without the Name one dies, my Master, as an addict craves for his drug.
Those in whose minds love for the Lord has taken hold: theirs is the fortune written of old, from the very start.
Moment by moment we serve the feet of those who find the Lord sweet.
My Master, the Lord, Har Har, has shown grace, and has united with himself the servant long separated.
Blessed, blessed is the True Guru, who has fixed the Name firmly within; servant Nanak is a sacrifice to him. ॥4॥
697.2: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
I have found the True Guru, my friend, the great Being; with relish upon relish the fruit of the Lord has come to me.
The serpent Maya has seized the mortal; through the Guru's words the Lord draws out the poison.
My mind is held by the sweet essence of the Lord's Name.
The Lord has made the fallen pure; meeting the Guru, the Saadh, they have tasted the Lord's sweet essence in the Lord's Name.
Blessed, blessed is the great good fortune by which the Guru, the Saadh, is met; meeting the Saadh, the attention rests in the state of unman (the mind raised above the world).
The fire of craving is quenched and peace is found, singing the pure, the utterly pure virtues of the Lord.
Meagre was the fortune set from the start for those who have not had the sight of the True Guru.
In the love of another they fall into womb after womb; their whole life passes in vain.
O Lord, give a spotless understanding, that we may serve the feet of the Guru, the Saadh, and the Lord may seem sweet to us.
Servant Nanak begs for the dust of the Saadh's feet; the Lord, becoming merciful, has it given. ॥4॥
697.3: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Those in whose hearts the Lord's Name has not come to dwell: better the Lord had made their mothers barren.
Their bodies wander empty, without the Name; they have worn themselves away and died, fretting and pining.
O my mind, repeat the Name of Ram, the Lord who dwells within.
The merciful Lord God, Har Har, showed mercy; the Guru gave wisdom, and the mind understood.
In Kalyug the Lord's praise is the highest state; it is through the True Guru that the Lord is found.
I give myself in sacrifice to my own True Guru, who has brought the hidden Name to light.
By great fortune the sight of the Saadh (the Guru) was granted, and all sins are lost and gone.
I have found the True Guru, the banker great in wisdom, who has made me a sharer in the Lord's many virtues.
Those on whom the Life of the world has shown mercy have enshrined the Lord in their hearts, within their minds.
At the door of Dharam Raj their papers were torn up; O servant Nanak, their account is settled. ॥4॥
698.1: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
By great fortune I have found the Sat Sangat (the company of the true) of the Saadh (the Guru); my wandering mind has come to rest.
Instruments ever play with the unstruck (anhat) melody; (the mind) has drunk its fill, with love, of the stream of the Lord's Amrit.
O my mind, repeat the Name of Ram, the beautiful Lord.
The True Guru has kindled love in my mind and body; the Lord has met me and clasped me in his embrace.
The Saakats (those who have turned from God) are bound fast in Maya; they hoard poison with all their might.
They cannot spend it for the Lord's sake, and they bear the pain of Jamkaal (death) upon their heads.
Those who have given their bodies over to the Lord, applying with deep faith the dust (of the feet) of the Guru, the Saadh, to their faces,
win glory from the Lord in this world and the next; the deep colour of the Lord's love has dyed their minds.
O Lord, Har Har, unite me, unite me with your servant, the Saadh (the Guru); I am a worm (a lowly servant) of the holy ones.
O servant Nanak, (one whose) love has taken hold for the feet of the Guru, the Saadh: meeting the Saadh, (that one's) foolish mind of stone has turned green. ॥4॥
698.2: Raag Jaitsri, Ghar 2, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Remember the Lord, Har Har, the unreachable, the infinite,
remembering whom our pain is erased.
O Lord, Har Har, unite (us) with the True Guru, the Being; when the Guru is met, there is peace.
Sing the Lord's virtues, my friends;
keep the Name of the Lord, Har Har, enshrined in the heart.
Recite to (me) the Amrit words of the Lord, Har Har; when the Guru is met, (the Lord) becomes manifest.
The Lord, Madhusudan, Madho, is my breath of life;
to my mind and body (his) Amrit tastes sweet.
O Lord, Har Har, show mercy and unite (me) with the Guru, that Being untouched by Maya (Niranjan).
The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is ever the giver of peace;
my mind is dyed in the Lord's love.
O Lord, Har Har, unite (me) with the Guru, the great Being; says Nanak: O Guru, through the Name there is peace. ॥4॥
698.3: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, Har Har;
through the Guru, ever earn the profit of the Naam.
Make devotion to the Lord, Har Har, firm within; the Name of the Lord, Har Har, (fills the mind with) eager delight.
Meditate on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, the merciful;
in the Lord's love, ever sing (his) virtues.
Dance the ghoomar of the praise of the Lord, Har Har; joining the Sat Sangat, there is eager delight.
Come, my companions, let us meet in union with the Lord;
hearing the Lord's discourse, earn the profit of the Naam.
Show mercy, O Lord, Har Har, and unite (us) with the Guru; when the Guru is met, there is eager delight for the Lord.
Singing the praise and glory of the unreachable, the unfathomable (Lord),
sing the Name of Ram at every moment.
O Guru, the giver, show mercy and meet me; Nanak's eager delight is in devotion to the Lord. ॥4॥
699.1: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
With delight upon delight we praise the Lord (Ram), the fount of all sweetness;
the mind is drenched in the Lord's Name and earns the profit.
Moment by moment, day and night, we perform devotion; through the Guru's teaching there is eager delight in devotion.
We repeat the virtues of Govind (the Lord of the universe), the Lord, Har Har;
conquering mind and body, we earn the profit of the Shabad.
Through the Guru's teaching the five enemies (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) come under control; in mind and body there is eager delight for the Lord.
The Naam is a jewel; we repeat the Lord's Name;
singing the Lord's virtues, we ever earn the profit.
O Madho, merciful to the meek, show mercy, (that there may be) eager delight for the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Again and again I repeat (the Name of) the Lord of the world (Jagdish) within my mind;
the Lord, Har Har, the Master of the world, is the (true) profit in the world.
Blessed, blessed are you, my great Master, my God; repeating (your Name), Nanak has eager delight in devotion. ॥4॥
699.2: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
He himself is the yogi, and the way (of yoga), through all the ages;
he himself, the fearless, sits rapt in trance.
He himself alone is at work in all; he himself (gives) eager delight in the Name.
He himself is the continents (dweep) and the worlds, and he gives them light;
he himself is the True Guru and the ocean, and he churns it.
He himself, churning and churning, has the essence drawn out; repeating the jewel of the Name, there is eager delight.
Come together, my companions; together let us sing (his) virtues;
through the Guru, repeat the Naam: (this is) the profit of the Lord.
(One in whom) devotion to the Lord, Har Har, is made firm and is pleasing to the mind: (to that one) the Name of the Lord, Har Har, brings eager delight.
He himself is the great, wise one, the great banker;
through the Guru, buy the capital of the Naam.
O Lord, Har Har, O God, grant this gift, as it pleases you: for Nanak, (your) virtues, (your) Name and eager delight (in it). ॥4॥
699.3: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Joining the Sat Sangat, in the company of the Guru,
let us buy, through the Guru, the capital of the Naam.
O Lord, Har Har, O Madhusudan, show mercy, that joining the Sat Sangat, there may be eager delight.
May we hear with our ears the Bani of the Lord's virtues;
in your mercy, unite (us) with the True Guru.
May we sing (your) virtues and speak (your) virtues through the Bani; repeating the Lord's virtues, there is eager delight.
If all pilgrimages, fasts, sacrificial rites and acts of charity are weighed,
they never come up to the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Beyond all weighing is the Lord, Har Har; his weight is exceedingly great; repeating (him) through the Guru's teaching, there is eager delight.
May we repeat the Lord's Name: (it is) all rites and righteous deeds;
(it) washes away the filth of sins and misdeeds.
O you who are merciful to the meek, be kind to your servant; give Nanak the Name and eager delight (in it). ॥4॥
700.1: Raag Jaitsri, Ghar 3, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Rare is the one who knows who is a (true) friend here in this world.
Only one on whom (God) is merciful understands the way of it; that one's way of life is pure.
Mother, father, wife, sons, kin, dear friends and brothers
have come together through the ties of past births; at the end, none of them is any help.
Strings of pearls, gold, rubies and diamonds, the wealth that charms the mind:
crying out for (them), one's span of life has passed, yet in them no contentment was found.
Elephants, chariots, horses swift as the wind, (one may be) a man of wealth, a lord of lands, (master of) an army of four wings,
yet none of these went along with him at all; he rose and departed naked.
The Lord's Sants are the dear beloveds of God; in their company one should sing (the praise of) the Lord, Har Har.
O Nanak, peace here and a radiant face hereafter are found in the company of the Sants. ॥4॥
700.2: Raag Jaitsri, Ghar 3, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Give me word, tell me, tell me of the Beloved.
Hearing (of him) in so many ways, I am bewildered; tell me, O happy soul-brides, my companions.
Some say he is outside all, far beyond; some say he is within all.
No colour of his is seen, no mark of his is discerned; O happy soul-brides, help me understand the truth.
He dwells in all, he lives in every heart, and yet no stain touches him, not in the least.
Says Nanak: listen, O people, he dwells upon the tongue of the Sants. ॥2॥
700.3: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Hearing of God, I take heart, I take heart.
Seeing God near, close at hand, I offer (him) my soul, my breath, my mind, my body, everything.
He is countless, endless, the great Giver; seeing God, I hold him fast in my mind.
Whatever I wish for, that very thing I receive; meditating on God, I fulfil my hopes and longings.
By the Guru's grace (God) has come to dwell in Nanak's mind; having understood God, I never pine in any sorrow. ॥4॥
700.4: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
My Friend is the one for whom (all) long.
In every home sing beautiful songs of joy (to him); in every heart he has his dwelling.
Worship him in joy, worship him in sorrow; may he not be forgotten at any time.
Repeating the Naam brings the light of millions of suns, and doubt's darkness is destroyed.
(O God,) in every place and every space between, in all places (you are); whatever is seen is yours.
O Nanak, whoever finds (God) in the company of the Sants never again goes round (in birth and death). ॥2॥
701.1: Raag Jaitsri, Ghar 4, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Now I have found peace by the Guru's command.
I have given up cleverness, put worry out of mind, and cast off ego and left it behind.
When I look, I see all bewitched by attachment; so I ran and fell at the Guru's refuge.
In his mercy the Lord set me to his service; then Jam (the messenger of Death) let go of me.
I crossed the ocean of fire when, by great fortune, I met the Sants.
Servant Nanak has found every comfort, for my mind is fixed on the Lord's feet. ॥2॥
701.2: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I have fixed my attention on the True Guru in my mind;
I have made firm (within me) the wisdom and the mantra of the Lord's Name; God has shown me mercy.
The nets of death, the great entanglements and the fear of Jam are gone.
I have come to the refuge of the remover of sorrow, the Lord of compassion, and have taken hold of (his) feet as (my) support.
The Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) has become a boat, (and I) have crossed the ocean of the world.
Says Nanak, I have drunk the Amrit (of the Name), doubt is gone, and I have borne the unbearable. ॥2॥
701.3: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those for whom Govind has become the helper
have every comfort, Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise) and bliss with them; no ailment touches them.
They are seen with everyone, yet stay untouched; Maya has no hold on them.
Dyed in the love of the One, they know the essence; they have received this understanding from the True Guru.
Those on whom the Master's kindness, compassion and grace rest are the Sants of loving heart.
O Nanak, in the company of those who have sung the Lord's praises with relish and delight, one is carried across. ॥2॥
701.4: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Gobind, you are the life, the breath, the wealth and the beauty (of all beings);
for creatures sunk deep in ignorance and attachment, you are a lamp in the darkness.
O beloved God, the sight of you bears fruit; (your) lotus feet are beyond compare.
Countless times I bow to them, and offer my very mind (before them) as incense.
Worn out, I have fallen at your door, O God, and have taken firm hold of your shelter.
Pull Nanak, your own, out of the pit of the world's fire. ॥2॥
701.5: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
If only some servant (of God) would join me to the Lord,
I would clasp his feet, speak kind words (to him) with my tongue, and my very life would be given (to him) as an offering.
(A rare one) makes mind and body a pure garden-bed and waters it well with the Lord's nectar;
by (God's) grace, breaking away from the great poison of Maya, he is absorbed in this relish.
O destroyer of the sorrows of the meek, I have come to your refuge; I turn my thoughts to you (alone).
O God, undo Nanak's bonds and (grant him) the gift of the fearless state and of the Master's remembrance. ॥2॥
702.1: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
As the chatrik longs for the rain to pour, (so I long:)
O God, ocean of mercy, show compassion: (grant me) the longing for loving devotion to the Lord.
The chakvi does not want countless comforts; seeing the day (break), she is in perfect bliss.
By no other means does the fish live; without water, death is its lot.
O Lord, O Master, we who have no master are at your refuge: show your mercy.
Nanak worships (God's) lotus feet; without him, nothing else (is dear to him). ॥2॥
702.2: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
He who is my very life dwells in my mind and body;
in his mercy the Perfect Being, the all-knowing, has met me in the company of the Saadh (the Guru).
Those who have been given the stupefying herb of love have drunk the sweet essence in great measure.
Its worth cannot be told; what power have I (to tell it)?
(God) has fastened his servants to the hem of his robe; the Saviour has saved (them).
Remembering, remembering, remembering God, Nanak has found peace at the refuge of (his) door. ॥2॥
702.3: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
After wandering through countless births, we have come to (your) refuge.
Save (us) from the blind well of (attachment to) the body, and attach (us) to your feet.
I know nothing of wisdom, meditation or (righteous) deeds; my conduct is not pure.
Attach (me) to the hem of the Saadh Sangat, so that the treacherous river may be crossed.
Comforts, wealth, the sweet pleasures of Maya: these are not to be kept in the mind.
Servant Nanak finds his fill in the sight of the Lord; the love of the Lord's Name is (his) ornament. ॥2॥
702.4: Raag Jaitsri, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O servants of the Lord, remember Ram in your hearts.
Misfortune does not come near the Lord's servant; all the tasks of (such) a servant are fulfilled.
Through the Lord's service millions of obstacles are destroyed, (and) the eternal abode of Govind (is reached).
The devotee of the Lord has no fear at all; (even) Jam pays him honour.
Forsaking Gopal (the Lord who sustains all), whatever else is done is unsound, and every bit of it perishes.
O Nanak, hold (God's) lotus feet in your heart; (in them) all comforts find their home. ॥2॥
702.5: Raag Jaitsri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The mind has gone astray, entangled in Maya.
Whatever deeds it did, driven by greed, by each of them it bound itself.
It did not understand; absorbed in the pleasures of the senses, it forgot the Lord's praise.
The Master is with it, but it did not know him; it ran off to search the forests.
Ram, the jewel, is within the heart itself, yet it did not gain the knowledge of him.
O servant Nanak, without worship of the Lord it has wasted its life in vain. ॥2॥
703.1: Raag Jaitsri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
O dear Lord, save my honour.
The dread of Jam has entered my heart; O treasure of mercy, I have taken hold of your refuge.
I am a great sinner, a fool, and greedy too; committing sins, I am now worn out.
The fear of dying never leaves my mind; that worry has burnt up my body.
I tried (many) means to be set free, and rose and ran in all ten directions.
The Stainless One dwells within the heart itself, (yet) I have not found his secret.
I have no virtue, no chanting or austerity at all; what deed should now be done?
Nanak, worn out, has fallen at (your) refuge; O God, grant the gift of fearlessness. ॥3॥
703.2: Raag Jaitsri, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
O mind, hold fast to this true reflection:
know that without the Name of Ram this whole world is false.
He whom the yogis searched for until they were worn out, and did not find his limit:
recognise that Master as near you; he is beyond form and feature.
The Name of the Lord is the purifier in the world, (yet) you have never kept it in mind.
O you to whom the world bows, Nanak has fallen at (your) refuge; keep to your age-old way (of grace). ॥2॥
703.3: Raag Jaitsri, Ghar 1, a Chhant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Thirsting for (his) sight, day and night, every day, always, I think of him.
O Nanak, opening the doors (of my mind), the Guru has united me with the Lord, my Friend. ॥1॥
703.4: Listen, my friend, my dear one: I make one request.
I wander searching for that enchanting, darling Beloved.
Tell me of that Beloved, and I would cut off my head and lay it (before you); let me have (his) sight even for a moment.
My eyes are dyed in the colour of the Beloved's love; (without him) I cannot be at peace even for an instant.
My mind is absorbed in God as the fish in water; I thirst like the chatrik.
Servant Nanak has found the Perfect Guru, and all thirst is quenched.
O friend, all the Beloved's companions (are such that) I am like none of them.
O friend, each surpasses the other; in whose thoughts am I?
(God's) many loved ones, each surpassing the other, always enjoy the delights (of union with him).
Seeing them, a longing rises in my mind: when shall I find the treasure of virtues?
To the one who has won my Darling's pleasure I would give my mind.
Says Nanak, O happy soul-bride, hear my plea: tell me, let me see, what is the Husband like?
O friend, the Husband does as he himself wills; he depends on no one at all.
O friend, you have enjoyed (union with) the Darling: I ask you, tell me.
You have found the Darling by losing self; (he is found by) the bride on whose forehead good fortune is (written).
(The happy soul-bride says:) The Master took me by the arm and made me his own; he did not weigh my virtues and faults.
(O Lord,) she whom you have adorned with the necklace of virtues and dyed in the deep red of (your love), on her everything looks lovely.
O servant Nanak, blessed is that happy soul-bride with whom the Husband dwells.
O friend, the wish I always made in my prayers, that I have received.
The Groom I longed for has come, and the songs of rejoicing ring out.
Great joy and delight have come; the Husband is kind and ever fresh in his love.
By great fortune I found him; the Guru brought me (to him) in the true company of the Saadh.
All my hopes and longings are fulfilled; the Beloved has clasped me in his embrace.
Nanak prays: the wish I made in my prayers, that I have received by meeting the Guru. ॥4॥
704.1: Raag Jaitsri, Ghar 2, a Chhant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
God is lofty, beyond reach and boundless; the Indescribable cannot be described.
Nanak has come to the refuge of God, who has the power to protect.
As you see fit, O Lord God, so protect (me): I am yours.
How many can I count? My faults are countless.
Countless are the faults, the sins and the rounds (they bring); every day, always, we go astray.
We stay sunk in attachment to dreadful Maya; by your grace alone are we set free.
In secret we commit grievous wrongs, (yet) God is nearer than the nearest.
Nanak prays: show mercy, and pull (us) out of the whirlpools of the world-ocean.
(God's) countless virtues cannot be assessed; lofty is the Name of God.
This is Nanak's prayer: may (I,) who have no place, find a place.
There is no other place; to whom else should one go?
At all hours, with joined palms, one should meditate on that God.
Meditating always on that God of ours, one receives what the mind desires.
Giving up pride, attachment and the sin of (leaning on) another, one should fix one's attention on the One.
Offering mind and body before God, one should erase all self.
Nanak prays: (O God,) show mercy, (that we may) stay merged in (your) True Name.
O mind, one should meditate on him in whose hands is every means.
O Nanak, one should gather the wealth of the Name of Ram; it goes with one to the end.
God alone is the dear companion; there is no other.
He himself is in every place and every space between; he fills the water and the land.
God the Master, the Giver to all, pervades the water, the land and the sky.
Gopal, Gobind has no end; his virtues are endless: how can I count them?
Hasten to the refuge of the Master, the bringer of peace; besides him there is none.
Nanak prays: (O God,) the one on whom you show mercy obtains the Naam.
Whatever I wished for in my mind, that I have received.
Meditating on the Naam, Nanak (has found) all comforts.
Now, joining the company of the Saadh (the Guru), the mind is set free.
Those who through the Guru have taken up the Naam have had their light merge in the Light.
Remembering the Lord's Name, (their) sins are erased; the burning is quenched, and (the mind) is filled.
In his kindness (God) has taken them by the arm, made them his own and given them honour.
The Lord has clasped them to himself and united them (with him); the pains of birth and death are burnt away.
Nanak prays: (God) has shown mercy and united (them with himself) in an instant. ॥4॥
705.1: Raag Jaitsri, a Chhant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The world is a traveller passing through, yet it is smeared with pride;
steeped in the colours of Maya, people commit countless sins.
Sunk in greed, attachment and arrogance, they never think of death;
sons, friends, dealings and wife: tending to these, their life slips by.
When the days written for them are over, O mother, they suffer at the sight of Dharam Raj's messengers.
The deeds they have done are not wiped away; O Nanak, the wealth of the Lord's Name they have not earned.
They make countless efforts, but do not sing the Lord's Name;
they wander through countless births, dying, being born and coming again.
Beasts, birds, stones and trees: (such births) are beyond all counting.
Whatever seed you sow, its fruits you will enjoy; each one receives what he himself has done.
Those who lose the jewel of this life in a gamble are not pleasing to God himself.
Nanak prays: led astray, they wander, and find no resting place even for an instant.
Youth has gone by, and old age has seized its place and settled in;
his hands tremble, his head wobbles, and his eyes no longer see.
Nothing is seen by the eyes; without worship of the Lord, he leaves Maya behind and departs.
They do not heed his word and throw dust on his head, those for whose sake he burned his mind and body.
The love of the Lord (Sri Ram), boundless and all-pervading, did not dwell in his mind even for an instant.
Nanak prays: like millions of sheets of paper (in a fire), this false (body) takes no time to perish.
Nanak has come to the refuge of the lotus feet (of the Lord);
God himself has carried (us) across the world, so full of fears and so hard to cross.
Joining the Saadh Sangat, we worshipped Sridhar (the Lord); taking our side, dear God carried (us) across.
The Lord accepted (us) and gave (us) the Name; he weighed nothing else (of ours).
The treasure of virtues, the boundless Master, the One our mind longed for, we have found.
Nanak prays: having eaten the food of the Lord's Name, we are satisfied forever. ॥4॥
705.2: Raag Jaitsri Vaar: by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji), with saloks.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
At the beginning the Supreme God is present everywhere, in the middle present everywhere, and at the end present everywhere.
The Sants remember the One who pervades all places; O Nanak, the Lord of the world is the destroyer of sins. ॥1॥
706.1: In seeing, hearing and telling (of him), let the True One be fixed firmly in the mind;
he pervades all places; O Nanak, merge in the love of the Lord. ॥2॥
706.2: Let the One Lord, Niranjan, be sung; he alone is within all.
God is the Cause of creation, all-powerful; whatever he does comes to pass.
In an instant he sets up and pulls down; there is none but him.
He pervades the continents, the universes, the nether worlds, the islands and all the worlds.
He alone understands whom (God) himself makes understand; that one is a pure servant. ॥1॥
706.3: (God) fashions the frame of beings and places them in the mother's womb;
with every breath they remember him, O Nanak, and the great fire (of the womb) does not destroy them. ॥1॥
706.4: With your face down and your feet up, you dwelt in that dreadful place;
says Nanak: why have you forgotten that Master, through whose Name you are saved? ॥2॥
706.5: Of blood and seed you sprouted, in the fire of the belly,
upside down, unclean and in distress, in a dreadful, pitch-dark hell.
Remembering the Lord, you did not burn (there); enshrine him in your mind, your body and your heart.
The One who brought you safe out of that hard place, do not forget him even a little.
Forgetting God there is never peace; you will depart having lost your life. ॥2॥
706.6: He grants the gifts the mind desires, and fulfils hopes everywhere;
he destroys strife and suffering; O Nanak, remember that God: he is not far. ॥1॥
706.7: The One in whose company you enjoy all pleasures: let love be formed with him.
May that Husband Lord, who fashioned the beautiful body, not be forgotten for an instant, O Nanak. ॥2॥
706.8: He gave (you) soul and breath, body and wealth; he gave delights to enjoy.
He gave houses, mansions, chariots and horses, arranging happy circumstances.
God, who is able to give, has given sons, wife, friends and servants.
Remembering the Lord, body and mind turn green, and the pains of separation are lifted.
In the Saadh Sangat, dwell on the Lord's virtues; (so) all ailments are destroyed. ॥3॥
706.9: People strive for their family and make countless endeavours for Maya,
but are empty of loving devotion to the Lord; O Nanak, those who forget God are ghosts. ॥1॥
706.10: Broken is the love that was formed with another;
O Nanak, the true way is to be steeped in (the love of) the Master. ॥2॥
706.11: When the (life) leaves it, the body turns to ash, and all call it a ghost;
those with whom there was such love do not let it stay in the house even for an instant.
He amassed wealth by doing wrong; of what use is it (now)?
As one sows, so one reaps; this (body) is the field of deeds.
The ungrateful have forgotten the Lord, and wander through births. ॥4॥
706.12: (They gain the fruit of) millions of gifts in charity and holy bathings, and of countless rites of cleansing and purity,
who utter Har Har with the tongue, O Nanak; they are freed from all sins. ॥1॥
706.13: I piled up a great heap of firewood and set a little fire to it (and it all burned away);
just so, O Nanak, when the True Husband Lord dwells in the mind, all sorrows are taken away. ॥2॥
707.1: Millions of sins, every one of them, perish in remembering the Lord's Name;
the fruits the mind longs for are obtained by singing the Lord's virtues;
the fears of birth and death are cut away, (and one gains) the true place that never moves.
If it is so written from the beginning, one is absorbed in the Lord's feet.
O God, show grace and keep (me) safe; Nanak is a sacrifice (to you). ॥5॥
